applies_why: The judge treats the cited verses' not stating that Joseph begat the child as support for holding the defense, which is the absence-of-statement reasoning K-S2 governs.
quote: While the challenger demonstrated that Davidic lineage is reckoned according to the flesh ([L1] Romans 1:3; [L3] Acts 2:30), neither text states that Joseph begat the child ([L4]). Because the defender answered the witnesses pressed against the chain and neither withdrew nor suffered refutation of the declared links, the defense holds ([L4]).
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.
room: Phrase: single verse does not state a link or its contrary. Reading one: any reliance on a verse's silence as support for holding is barred; reading two: only a solitary verse and only an express sole-ground for STANDS is barred. I take reading one because the judge relies on the silence of the cited verses.
why: The judge uses the fact that the cited texts do not state that Joseph begat the child as part of the basis for holding the defense, which K-S2 forbids.
